perspective:
Keith’s available information:

- Keith works at a construction company. Elizabeth is the receptionist there. They have a friendly but professional relationship, mainly through his office visits for paperwork and project updates.
- Recently Keith noticed Elizabeth being unusually curt with him over several days. He wondered if he had unknowingly upset her through a misunderstanding or mistake.
- Keith asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. She told him no, that she was dealing with personal stuff, and apologized if she seemed short.
- Keith felt sympathetic and wanted to support her. He told her he understood she was going through a tough time, offered to listen, and suggested a coffee break. Elizabeth accepted and thanked him.
- During coffee, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses. They seemed severe to Keith. He thought professional help might benefit her but worried about offending her, so he asked if she had considered talking to a professional.
- Elizabeth told Keith she had thought about it but was unsure and hesitant about seeking help.
- After that suggestion, Keith noticed Elizabeth become slightly withdrawn. He believed he might have embarrassed her and felt regretful. He told her he hoped he hadn’t overstepped and that he was there to support her. Elizabeth said he hadn’t overstepped, appreciated his concern, and said it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Elizabeth seemed more open and appreciative toward Keith. Keith believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him. He told her he was always available to chat or take a break together. Elizabeth thanked him, said it meant a lot, and said she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith intends to maintain this supportive relationship.

Keith does not have access to any information beyond what he observed, heard from Elizabeth, said himself, or already knew from their prior colleague interactions.
